title: Twenty First Word First Station Conclusion Wisdom In Calamity And Consolation Through Belief

questions.question: What happens to a big joy when a person thinks only about this world?
questions.answer: It turns into deep sadness.

questions.question: In the example, how many friends of the first man had already gone away?
questions.answer: Almost all of them, ninety-nine out of a hundred.

questions.question: Where had the first man’s friends gone?
questions.answer: They had gone to Istanbul.

questions.question: How does the first man think about the place where his friends went?
questions.answer: He thinks of it as a good place and wants to go there too.

questions.question: How does the first man feel when he is told that he can go there?
questions.answer: He becomes very happy.

questions.question: What does the first man do after hearing that he may go?
questions.answer: He goes gladly.

questions.question: What does the second man think happened to most of his friends?
questions.answer: He thinks they were lost in a sad way and are gone from him.

questions.question: How is the second man different from the first man in the way he understands separation?
questions.answer: The first sees it as going to join friends, but the second sees it as painful loss.

questions.question: What does the second man try to do with the one guest who remains?
questions.answer: He tries to become close to him for comfort.

questions.question: Why does the second man cling to that one guest?
questions.answer: He hopes it will help him forget the pain of missing the others.

questions.question: According to the passage, where are the Prophet and all of a person’s friends now?
questions.answer: They are beyond the grave.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the one or two people who are still alive?
questions.answer: They will also go there later.

questions.question: What feeling about death does the passage tell the nafs not to have?
questions.answer: It says not to be scared of death.

questions.question: What feeling about the grave does the passage tell the nafs not to have?
questions.answer: It says not to be worried about the grave.

questions.question: What brave attitude should a person have toward death and the grave?
questions.answer: A person should face them bravely and not turn away.

questions.question: Which of the two men should a person avoid copying?
questions.answer: The second man.

questions.question: What excuse about modern times does the passage reject?
questions.answer: The excuse that this age is different and everyone is too busy with worldly life.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does not change even when times change?
questions.answer: Death, separation, human weakness, and human need do not change.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to human weakness and need?
questions.answer: They grow more, not less.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the human journey through life?
questions.answer: It does not stop; it moves even faster.

questions.question: Why is saying “I am like everyone else” not a real comfort?
questions.answer: Because people stay with you only up to the grave.

questions.question: Why does the passage say that sharing trouble with everyone else is not enough?
questions.answer: Because after the grave that kind of comfort no longer helps.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the world when seen with wisdom?
questions.answer: It is full of order and purpose.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about earthquakes and similar events?
questions.answer: They are not meaningless accidents.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the earth and living things as signs of order?
questions.answer: It says the world is dressed with carefully arranged creatures and moves in a planned way.

questions.question: What mistake is made by calling painful events pure chance and without purpose?
questions.answer: It wrongly removes wisdom, mercy, and justice from those events.

questions.question: What can happen to the lost property of believers during such events?
questions.answer: It can become like charity and gain lasting reward.

questions.question: How can these hard events benefit believers spiritually?
questions.answer: They can wipe away sins that came from not being thankful enough.

questions.question: What future picture of the earth is given near the end of the passage?
questions.answer: The earth will one day clear away corrupt deeds from its surface.

questions.question: What welcome will be given to thankful people?
questions.answer: They will be invited to enter Paradise.

questions.question: What is the main warning at the start of the passage about loving only worldly life?
questions.answer: Focusing only on this life can make a person suffer badly.

questions.question: In the story, what is the first man’s view of the place where his friends have gone?
questions.answer: He sees it as a place of reunion and happiness.

questions.question: What shows that the first man has hope?
questions.answer: He looks forward to joining his friends and is glad to go.

questions.question: What wrong idea does the second man have about those who left?
questions.answer: He thinks they are gone into misery and cut off completely.

questions.question: How does that wrong idea affect the second man’s heart?
questions.answer: It leaves him sad and desperate.

questions.question: What small thing does the second man use to cover a huge sorrow?
questions.answer: He tries to take comfort in one remaining guest.

questions.question: Why is the second man called wretched in the example?
questions.answer: Because he misunderstands what happened and suffers needlessly.

questions.question: Who is mentioned first among those beyond the grave?
questions.answer: Allah’s Beloved, the Prophet.

questions.question: What truth about loved ones is the nafs told to remember?
questions.answer: Loved ones have gone ahead beyond the grave, and the rest will follow.

questions.question: What should a person do instead of turning away from the grave?
questions.answer: Face it with courage and think about what it really means.

questions.question: What lesson is taught by saying to laugh in death’s face?
questions.answer: A believer should meet death with bravery, not panic.

questions.question: Which kind of person is warned against becoming like?
questions.answer: A person who is heedless and thinks like the second man.

questions.question: What common excuse about the age is answered in the passage?
questions.answer: The claim that people today are too wrapped up in worldly struggle to think differently.

questions.question: According to the passage, does death become less real in a busy age?
questions.answer: No, it stays the same.

questions.question: Does separation turn into staying forever just because time has changed?
questions.answer: No, it does not.

questions.question: What happens to human helplessness and need over time?
questions.answer: They increase.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the speed of the human journey?
questions.answer: It becomes quicker.

questions.question: Why is “everyone is like me” a weak excuse?
questions.answer: Because other people cannot stay with you past the grave.

questions.question: How far does ordinary friendship go, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It reaches only to the grave.

questions.question: What does the eye of wisdom help a person notice in the world?
questions.answer: That everything is arranged with order and purpose.

questions.question: If the world is ordered and meaningful, what does that say about human life?
questions.answer: Human life is also not outside that order and purpose.

questions.question: What example from nature is used to show careful planning?
questions.answer: The many kinds of animals and plants spread over the earth in beautiful order.

questions.question: What image is used to describe the earth’s movement?
questions.answer: It is compared to a whirling dervish moving in order toward high goals.

questions.question: What opinion about earthquakes is rejected?
questions.answer: The idea that they are random and meaningless.

questions.question: According to the passage, what might the earth be doing through such shaking?
questions.answer: It may be casting off forms of human heedlessness it rejects.

questions.question: Why is it especially serious when believers are heedless?
questions.answer: Because they should be people of faith and thankfulness.

questions.question: Why is it wrong to say the losses of sufferers are for nothing?
questions.answer: Because that view throws people into hopeless fear and ignores divine wisdom.

questions.question: Under whose command do such events happen?
questions.answer: They happen by the command of Allah, who is Wise and Compassionate.

questions.question: What reward can come from the temporary belongings believers lose?
questions.answer: Those losses can be turned into lasting reward like charity.

questions.question: What two different endings are described for two groups of people?
questions.answer: Those who associate partners with Allah are driven to Hell, while thankful people are called to Paradise.

questions.question: What big idea is taught through the example of the two men?
questions.answer: The way a person understands death and separation changes whether he feels hope or pain.

questions.question: Why is the first man cheerful about leaving?
questions.answer: He believes he is going to join many dear friends in a good place.

questions.question: Why does the first man’s sadness not control him?
questions.answer: Because he sees the move as reunion, not destruction.

questions.question: Why does the second man suffer more than the first?
questions.answer: Because he thinks separation means complete loss.

questions.question: What does the second man fail to understand about those who left?
questions.answer: He does not understand that departure is not the end.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest is a poor replacement for many lost friends?
questions.answer: Depending on one person for all comfort.

questions.question: In this passage, what does the grave seem to be for believers?
questions.answer: It seems like a passage to where loved ones have gone.

questions.question: How should this understanding change a believer’s view of death?
questions.answer: It should make the believer calmer and braver.

questions.question: What command tells the nafs not to run away from thinking about death?
questions.answer: It is told not to turn its head away.

questions.question: What does listening to what the grave wants mean in simple words?
questions.answer: It means thinking carefully about its message instead of ignoring it.

questions.question: What kind of character is encouraged by the words about bravery?
questions.answer: A strong and trusting character.

questions.question: What mistaken thought about modern life is answered next?
questions.answer: The thought that our time is so different that these truths no longer matter.

questions.question: Name one thing the passage says does not change with the times.
questions.answer: Death does not change.

questions.question: Name another thing the passage says does not change with the times.
questions.answer: Human need and weakness do not change.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the movement of life toward its end?
questions.answer: It keeps going and even speeds up.

questions.question: Why can’t a person depend on the crowd for lasting comfort?
questions.answer: Because the crowd cannot accompany him beyond the grave.

questions.question: What does the phrase about a guesthouse teach about the world?
questions.answer: This world is a temporary stopping place, not a permanent home.

questions.question: In the guesthouse of the world, what is wisdom able to see?
questions.answer: Wisdom sees arrangement, meaning, and purpose everywhere.

questions.question: What question does the passage ask about human beings and order?
questions.answer: If everything is within order, how could a person be outside it and meaningless?

questions.question: What natural event is discussed as an example?
questions.answer: An earthquake.

questions.question: What false explanation of earthquakes is criticized?
questions.answer: That they happen only by blind chance.

questions.question: How does the passage use the beauty of living things on earth in its argument?
questions.answer: It points to their careful design to show the world is not random.

questions.question: What does the passage say is wrong about claiming disaster victims’ losses are pointless?
questions.answer: It removes hope and treats their suffering unfairly.

questions.question: What spiritual value can come from a believer’s temporary losses?
questions.answer: They can gain permanent reward.

questions.question: What moral purpose can painful events serve for believers?
questions.answer: They can be a means of cleansing sins linked to thanklessness.

questions.question: What future change will happen when the earth dislikes human wrongdoing?
questions.answer: It will erase those corrupt works from its face.

questions.question: Which wrongdoing is especially mentioned as making deeds ugly?
questions.answer: Associating partners with Allah.

questions.question: What will happen to people who commit that wrongdoing and do not repent?
questions.answer: They will be cast into Hell.

questions.question: What will be said to people who are thankful?
questions.answer: They will be welcomed into Paradise.

questions.question: What overall feeling does the passage try to give believers?
questions.answer: Hope, courage, and trust in Allah’s wisdom.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is one harmful result of seeing only this worldly life?
questions.answer: A person’s joy can turn into painful sorrow.

questions.question: What number is repeated in the example to show that almost all the friends are gone?
questions.answer: Ninety-nine out of a hundred.

questions.question: What makes the first man eager instead of crushed?
questions.answer: He expects to meet his friends again.

questions.question: How does the first man react to news of his own departure?
questions.answer: He welcomes it happily.

questions.question: What sad belief controls the second man’s thinking?
questions.answer: He thinks those who left are gone in a hopeless way.

questions.question: What does the second man try to use as comfort?
questions.answer: The company of one remaining person.

questions.question: Why does that comfort not solve his real problem?
questions.answer: Because his real pain comes from his wrong understanding of separation.

questions.question: What loved person is mentioned first as already beyond the grave?
questions.answer: The Prophet.

questions.question: What truth about the living does the passage remind the nafs of?
questions.answer: The few who remain alive will also die and go on.

questions.question: What three reactions are believers told to avoid toward death and the grave?
questions.answer: Fear, anxiety, and turning away.

questions.question: What three stronger actions are believers called to show instead?
questions.answer: Facing the grave, listening to its message, and meeting death bravely.

questions.question: Why is heedlessness dangerous in this passage?
questions.answer: It makes a person think like the second man and lose hope.

questions.question: What complaint beginning with “times have changed” is refused?
questions.answer: The claim that this age is too different for these truths to matter.

questions.question: What permanent reality does the passage repeat first in answer to that complaint?
questions.answer: Death remains death.

questions.question: What does the passage say separation does not become?
questions.answer: It does not become lasting stay.

questions.question: What human condition is said to grow instead of disappear?
questions.answer: Human helplessness and need.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the path of human life?
questions.answer: It keeps moving and becomes faster.

questions.question: Why should a person not think, “At least everyone is in the same trouble”?
questions.answer: Because that thought gives no help after the grave.

questions.question: In the image of the world as a guesthouse, what is implied about our stay here?
questions.answer: Our stay is temporary.

questions.question: What does wise looking show about things in the world?
questions.answer: Nothing is without arrangement and meaning.

questions.question: If nothing is pointless, what does that suggest about human events too?
questions.answer: They also happen with purpose.

questions.question: What clothing image is used for the many creatures on earth?
questions.answer: They are described like layers of beautifully made garments on the earth.

questions.question: How does this image support the passage’s message?
questions.answer: It shows careful design, not chaos.

questions.question: What movement of the earth is mentioned?
questions.answer: Its turning in an ordered way.

questions.question: Why is calling earthquakes mere accident a serious mistake?
questions.answer: Because it denies wisdom and mercy in creation.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest the earth may be rejecting?
questions.answer: Certain forms of human heedlessness and wrongdoing.

questions.question: What emotional harm comes from saying disaster losses have no reward?
questions.answer: It throws suffering people into terrible despair.

questions.question: What can lost wealth become for believers?
questions.answer: It can become reward like charity.

questions.question: How can hardship be linked to sins in the passage?
questions.answer: It can serve as payment for sins tied to not thanking Allah.

questions.question: What final contrast is made between those who are ungrateful and those who are thankful?
questions.answer: The ungrateful wrongdoers are driven to punishment, while the thankful are welcomed to Paradise.

questions.question: What change takes place in pleasure when someone limits his thoughts to worldly life only?
questions.answer: Pleasure changes into pain.

questions.question: In the example, what does the first man want most?
questions.answer: He wants to join his friends.

questions.question: Why does the first man think about Istanbul with longing?
questions.answer: Because his dear friends are there.

questions.question: What feeling fills the first man when he hears he may travel there?
questions.answer: Joy.

questions.question: What false picture does the second man create in his mind about those who left?
questions.answer: He imagines they are lost in misery with no hopeful future.

questions.question: How does that false picture affect the way he lives now?
questions.answer: It makes him sad and desperate, so he grabs at small comfort.

questions.question: What does the one remaining guest represent for the second man?
questions.answer: A weak attempt to replace many lost relationships.

questions.question: What important truth about the grave is taught to the nafs?
questions.answer: It is where loved ones have already gone ahead.

questions.question: How can remembering that truth help a believer?
questions.answer: It can reduce fear and give courage.

questions.question: What does the passage say to do instead of avoiding the subject of death?
questions.answer: Face it bravely and think about its meaning.

questions.question: What behavior shows a person is acting like the second man?
questions.answer: Being heedless and seeing death only as hopeless loss.

questions.question: What excuse based on society does the passage answer?
questions.answer: The excuse that everybody is busy with worldly life, so that is just normal.

questions.question: Why is that excuse not accepted?
questions.answer: Because the basic truths of death and human need still remain.

questions.question: What happens to man’s weakness according to the passage?
questions.answer: It increases.

questions.question: What happens to man’s poverty or need according to the passage?
questions.answer: It also increases.

questions.question: What happens to the human journey according to the passage?
questions.answer: It speeds up.

questions.question: What limit is placed on human companionship in this passage?
questions.answer: It goes only as far as the grave.

questions.question: Why is comfort from being “just like everyone else” called meaningless later on?
questions.answer: Because after death that shared condition does not help a person.

questions.question: What does a wise view of the world reveal?
questions.answer: That everything has order and purpose.

questions.question: How does the passage challenge the idea that a person can be meaningless or outside the plan?
questions.answer: It argues that if all things are ordered, a person cannot be outside that order.

questions.question: Which event is specifically brought up to discuss suffering?
questions.answer: An earthquake.

questions.question: What larger lesson is drawn from the detailed beauty of plants and animals?
questions.answer: The world is governed with wisdom.

questions.question: What does the orderly motion of the earth add to that lesson?
questions.answer: It shows even great movements follow a plan.

questions.question: What is unfair about saying disaster victims lost everything for nothing?
questions.answer: It strips away hope of reward and treats their suffering as useless.

questions.question: According to the passage, whose command stands behind such events?
questions.answer: The command of Allah.

questions.question: What two divine qualities are highlighted in connection with these events?
questions.answer: Wisdom and compassion.

questions.question: How can a believer’s temporary property become everlasting in reward?
questions.answer: It can be counted like charity given for Allah’s sake.

questions.question: How can suffering be a mercy for believers?
questions.answer: It can remove sins connected to thanklessness.

questions.question: What future cleansing of the earth is described?
questions.answer: The earth will remove ugly deeds that dishonor its surface.

questions.question: How are thankful people treated at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: They are invited into Paradise.

questions.question: What is the first lesson taught in the passage about focusing only on this life?
questions.answer: It changes happiness into sorrow.

questions.question: How does the first man understand the departure of his friends?
questions.answer: He understands it as going to a place where they continue to live.

questions.question: Why is the first man glad to leave when his time comes?
questions.answer: He expects reunion, not ruin.

questions.question: How does the second man understand the departure of his friends?
questions.answer: He sees it as complete loss and misery.

questions.question: What emotional result comes from the second man’s way of thinking?
questions.answer: He is filled with grief.

questions.question: What does he try to use as a substitute for the many friends who left?
questions.answer: He tries to find comfort in one guest.

questions.question: What does this comparison teach about wrong beliefs?
questions.answer: Wrong beliefs can make a person suffer much more.

questions.question: Who is named as being beyond the grave before all other friends are mentioned?
questions.answer: The Prophet.

questions.question: What does the passage say will happen to the few people still left here?
questions.answer: They too will pass on there.

questions.question: What attitude should replace fear of death?
questions.answer: Brave acceptance and trust.

questions.question: What should replace worry about the grave?
questions.answer: Careful attention to its message.

questions.question: What kind of person does the passage warn the nafs not to resemble?
questions.answer: A heedless person who misunderstands death.

questions.question: What modern-sounding statement does the passage tell the nafs not to make?
questions.answer: That this age is different and everyone is absorbed in worldly living.

questions.question: What four realities are said to stay true despite changing times?
questions.answer: Death remains, separation remains, human helplessness remains, and human need remains.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the speed of life’s journey?
questions.answer: It increases.

questions.question: Why is copying the crowd not a safe guide?
questions.answer: Because the crowd can only accompany a person to the grave.

questions.question: What image shows that life in this world is temporary?
questions.answer: The world is described as a guesthouse.

questions.question: What does a wise person notice in this guesthouse?
questions.answer: He notices that everything is arranged with meaning.

questions.question: What question in the passage challenges the idea of being purposeless?
questions.answer: If all things are ordered, how could a person alone be outside that order?

questions.question: What worldly event is used to discuss divine wisdom in painful times?
questions.answer: An earthquake.

questions.question: How does the beauty and order of creatures on earth support belief in purpose?
questions.answer: Their careful arrangement shows planning and wisdom.

questions.question: What comparison is used for the earth’s movement?
questions.answer: It is compared to a whirling dervish moving in order.

questions.question: What belief about disasters is strongly rejected?
questions.answer: That they are random games of chance.

questions.question: What might the earth’s shaking symbolize in the passage?
questions.answer: A rejection of certain human heedlessness and sins.

questions.question: Why is saying losses are unrewarded called both an error and a wrong?
questions.answer: Because it is false and it pushes hurting people toward despair.

questions.question: What can Allah turn believers’ temporary losses into?
questions.answer: Into lasting reward like almsgiving.

questions.question: What past wrong can such hardships help erase?
questions.answer: Sins that came from failing to thank Allah properly.

questions.question: What will the earth eventually do to human works stained by shirk?
questions.answer: It will wipe them away from its face.

questions.question: What will happen to those who associate partners with Allah?
questions.answer: They will be thrown into Hell.

questions.question: What will happen to those who are thankful?
questions.answer: They will be called to enter Paradise.
